title: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Connector/J: Rogue server can drive large heap allocations from server-declared lengths in OK packets
summary:
Summary

MariaDB Connector/J sized heap allocations from lengths declared by the server in OK packets before checking that those lengths fit in the packet. A rogue or MitM server can make the client allocate megabytes from a packet of a few bytes.

Details

When CLIENT_SESSION_TRACK is negotiated (the default), an OK packet carries an info field followed by session-state blocks, each tracked variable being sent as a length-encoded name and value. OkPacket.parse() and parseWithInfo() allocated new byte[len] for the info field, the variable name and the value with the server-declared len, then copied the packet data into it. The copy failed with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsEx
summary_ko: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Con

title: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Connector/J: Length-encoded integers larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE were truncated before being used as lengths
summary:
Summary

MariaDB Connector/J narrowed 8-byte length-encoded integers received from the server to int without validation. A rogue or MitM server can send a value above Integer.MAX_VALUE whose truncation becomes a negative or arbitrary length.

Details

The protocol encodes lengths as length-encoded integers, whose 8-byte form the decoder (readLength() and readIntLengthEncodedNotNull()) returned as (int) readLong(). A value above Integer.MAX_VALUE therefore wrapped to a negative or unrelated int, used afterwards as a length to size allocations or reads, which ended in NegativeArraySizeException, out-of-bounds exceptions or oversized alloca
summary_ko: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Con

title: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Connector/J: XA recover() trusted server-supplied gtrid and bqual lengths
summary:
Summary

XAResource.recover() in MariaDB Connector/J trusted the gtrid_length and bqual_length columns returned by XA RECOVER to allocate and split each Xid.

Details

MariaDbPoolConnection and MariaDbPoolPinnedConnection built each Xid of the recovery list by allocating new byte[gtrid_length] and new byte[bqual_length] and copying from the data column, without validating the lengths against the XA specification bounds (Xid.MAXGTRIDSIZE, Xid.MAXBQUALSIZE) or the actual payload. Negative or oversized lengths, or lengths that do not fit the data, ended in large allocations or unchecked ex
summary_ko: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Con

title: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Connector/J: LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE file check could be satisfied by text inside quoted identifiers, letting a malicious server read client files
summary:
Summary

MariaDB Connector/J checked a server's LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE file request by searching the text of the command it had sent for LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE '<file>'. The search also matched inside quoted identifiers, string literals and comments, so text returned by the server and re-used in a later query could satisfy it. A rogue or MitM server can read any file the client JVM can read.

Details

When a server answers a command with a LOCAL INFILE request (0xFB packet), the connector opens the named file on the client host and streams it to the server, after verifying that the file corresponds to a LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE of the command it sent (ClientMessage.validateLocalFileName()
summary_ko: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Con

title: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Connector/J: Server could switch character_set_results away from UTF-8 without the client noticing
summary:
Summary

MariaDB Connector/J decodes every result as UTF-8 and guards character_set_client against a change to another charset, but did not guard character_set_results, and relied on the server's global session_track_system_variables list to be told about charset changes at all.

Details

The connector learns about session variable changes through session tracking, and closes the connection when character_set_client is switched away from UTF-8, so that its UTF-8 decoding stays correct. Two gaps remained:

  • character_set_results was not guarded: a server could switch it to another charset, after which the bytes of every result were decoded as UTF-8 although encoded
summary_ko: [org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client] MariaDB Con
